items.title: Argentinië wil vertrokken assistent niet vervangen, behalve als Messi wil
items.summary: Het voetbaljaar zit er binnenkort op voor de Argentijnse nationale ploeg en dan zal Walter Samuel na bijna tien jaar vertrekken als assistent-trainer. items.title: Janine van Wyk: ‘Our rooms were empty … no mattresses, no lightbulbs and not a drop of water’
items.summary: In an extract from the former South Africa captain’s book, she details less than ideal Wafcon 2006 preparations I was just a year into my international career when we qualified for my first Wafcon, which was then called the African Women’s Championship (AWC) and was held in Nigeria in 2006. I was extremely excited but very nervous to participate in this tournament, more so when it was announced that we would be in the same group as the hosts, and would play them last in the group. As it turned out, it would be the game that decided who finished top of the group. By then we had beaten Algeria 4-0 and Equatorial Guinea 2-0 and had to travel to Delta State to take on the hosts. I’d heard that Nigeria was the toughest country to travel to and I was about to realise why. It’s become common knowledge that South Africans and Nigerians are massive rivals on the football field but also don’t really get on off it. Continue reading...

items.title: Club Brugge bereikt akkoord met stad en kan stilaan aftellen naar nieuw stadion

items.title: "Une nomination catastrophique", "Il doit être viré" : Sébastien Pocognoli en bien fâcheuse posture
items.summary: Il y a quelques mois, la nomination de Sébastien Pocognoli comme sélectionneur de l’Écosse était encore présentée comme un énorme coup. La fédération écossaise affirmait avoir mené une vaste recherche internationale et se disait particulièrement satisfaite d’avoir attiré l’entraîneur belge. Entre-temps, l’enthousiasme a totalement disparu. Après une nouvelle lourde défaite, les doutes grandissent quant à sa méthode.

items.title: Max Dowman shines in England colours and sends another record tumbling
items.summary: Midfielder’s under-21s winner eclipsed Jude Bellingham’s mark and there was other talent to admire against France There may have been an Mbappé on the pitch – Ethan, the younger brother of Kylian, with whom he shares a near-identical gait – but by the end there was only one precocious talent on the lips of those watching England overcome France in their under-21s clash. Max Dowman had done it again, lighting up another game, this time in filthy conditions at Ashton Gate. It was fitting he had the final say in a 3-2 win. The noise that accompanied his match-winning goal? Well, beyond the palpable excitement in the stands in Bristol, that would be the sound of the teenager sending yet another record tumbling. Which one takes your fancy? Take your pick. At 14, playing for Arsenal’s under-19s, he became the Uefa Youth League’s youngest goalscorer. This time last year, after taking to the field at Slavia Prague aged 15 and 308 days, Dowman became the youngest player to feature in the Champions League. In March, six months on from his professional debut, he became the Premier League’s youngest goalscorer. He is the youngest player to earn a Premier League winner’s medal. Last month he was presented with three Guinness World Records. Continue reading...

items.title: Declan Rice agrees new Arsenal contract making him club’s joint highest-paid player
items.summary: Deal will run to 2031 and worth about £300,000 a week Jurriën Timber also agrees fresh contract extension Declan Rice has agreed a new five-year contract at Arsenal, with the England midfielder poised to match Bukayo Saka’s status as the highest-paid player at the Premier League champions. Representatives for Rice, who won his 82nd cap in England’s thrilling win over Spain on Sunday, have been in talks for months about extending the deal he signed in 2023 after a record £105m move from West Ham. That is believed to be worth about £250,000 a week and is due to expire in 2028, although Arsenal have the option of a further 12 months. Continue reading...

items.title: ‘He wants to change lives’: the story behind Bukayo Saka’s Sócrates award
items.summary: By supporting the non-profit BigShoe, the Arsenal forward has earned deserved plaudits for his social conscience Valerie Fiesser will never forget her surprise when Bukayo Saka contacted her out of the blue, asking whether he could help support a project in Nigeria in 2022. “I remember thinking: ‘Is this really Bukayo writing us an email?’” says the president of BigShoe, a non-profit organisation based in Frankfurt that has helped more than 10,000 children worldwide. “But that’s how he is. He’s always asking what more we can do.” Four years on from that unexpected email, Fiesser was given the secret task of reaching out for a letter for Saka to read from the podium when he was presented with the Sócrates award at last month’s Ballon d’Or ceremony in London for his humanitarian work. She got the words from Byiringiro, a 14-year-old from Rwanda who had his eyesight restored after having surgery thanks to BigShoe’s initiative. Continue reading...
